Guerrilla Missions are the ones that have replaced Abduction Missions in terms of consequences. They pop up only once per month as opposed to 3-4 times. The way they work narratively is that XCOM gets intel to disrupt some of the aliens activity and you can choose where to strike. If you do not, the aliens will finish the activity they are building towards. XCOM can only strike in regions you have control over though. A max of 3 missions will pop up at once and you have to choose one of them. As you guessed, them finishing their activity will negatively impact you. It is called a Dark Event. There are several types of Dark Events and they are randomly chosen. Some include: All Advent forces gain one armor for a month; Advent raids make rookies cost double for a month; Advents awareness goes up practically making concealment worthless for a month. Etc. Etc. You can see before hand which is which and then choose which one you want to prevent most. However, the consequences of the Dark Events, while certainly noticable, are very minor compared to the previous expansion. If theoretically all Dark Events came to pass it still wouldn't be a huge deal. Especially not if you are somewhat good at the game. This is a real tactics game. I love similar titles but that is much more of a puzzle game than anything else.  1. **Never dash**. If you uncover a new pod of enemies and you can't move anymore you'll have a bad time. Only exception is if you're concealed.  2. **Optimize your actions**. This means you take one action with every soldier (and check their options) and only after that take the final action with each one. Imagine moving a soldier and having a 25% and 45% chance to hit and you take the 45 one and miss. Then you move another soldier and realize he has a 100% chance to hit on the 45 guy. Bad order. Correct way is move the first guy, see the 45%, then move the second guy, see the 100% so take that shot and then switch back to either take the 25% shot or go on overwatch or something else.  3. **Increase your chances to hit**. By setting up flanks, removing cover with explosives and abilities, taking high ground and modding your weapons. If the average chance to hit you have is 70% and their average to hit you is 50% you should generally win because you hit/kill them way more.  4.**Care about your soldier's survival**. The best defense means killing everything before they have a chance to retaliate. If not possible though, or if it won't work, plan to keep your soldiers safe. Learn enemy behavior and damage amounts. If they have two active soldiers that can do 5 damage each and you can't kill them, check your soldiers position. Can your soldier be flanked? Yes > move to they can't. Does your soldier have at least 11 health? Yes > he is safe. No > he can die. Hunker down, use flashbangs, use smoke grenades, use Aid Protocol or something else that will increase his chances of survivial.  5. **Accept the reality of probability**. Anything less than 100% chance to hit **will** miss at some point. Do not ever count on a shot with less than 100% chance to hit.
